text:
matt (sales): FYI ACME asked for a hybrid deal — reserved GPU commits + per-token credits for burst. Their ask: how do we bill overages during seasonal spikes? they want predictable unit economics for budgeting.
anya (product): can you drop their expected monthly baseline + peak multiplier? also want to know if they expect rollover of unused credits.
matt (sales): baseline ~ 1.2B tokens/mo, but spikes up to 6x for 2w in Q4. asking for 12mo term, prefer some rollover, and a soft overage buffer.
leo (support): we've seen similar for FinX last year — they wanted a 20% grace for 3 months then overage. Ops had to manually pro-rate once. Painful.
ben (finance): high-level options: 1) blended effective rate across commit+overage (we model average), 2) grace buffer (credits + limited rollover) then overage at premium (e.g., 1.5x token rate), 3) automatic burst capacity with reserved warm pool charged at reserved rate but billed on usage. each has cashflow and accounting impacts.
anya (product): propose two product-friendly proposals to present: Option A (Predictable Blend): set committed tokens = baseline, embed an annualized blended rate that assumes X% seasonal uplift, no rollover. Option B (Commit + Buffer): committed tokens + 10% rolling buffer that can be used during spikes, unused buffer forfeited quarterly, overage billed at 1.4x.
matt (sales): ACME won't accept forfeiting all unused credits. they pushed for some rollover to next quarter. can we do quarterly rollover up to 25% of unused commit?
ben (finance): quarterly rollover up to 25% is workable if we limit total rollover exposure and require minimum monthly commit. need to model cash impact. I'll run scenarios.
anya (product): ok — action items: (1) ben to run three scenarios (blended, buffer+forfeit, buffer+25% quarterly rollover) with examples. (2) leo to surface any operational constraints (billing pro-rate complexity). (3) legal-ops to check contract language for rollover and grace. (4) product to draft recommended SLOs / launch guardrails.
ben (finance): I'll model tonight. sample scenario I'll share in-thread.
matt (sales): thanks — would be helpful to show ACME 3-year TCO for each option. they care about predictability more than lowest sticker.
anya (product): quick sketch to model — please sanity-check:
```
Scenario: baseline=1.2B tokens/mo, peak window=2w at 6x baseline (12B tokens), commit=1.5B/mo, buffer=10% commit, rollover cap=25%/quarter.
Compute billed tokens by month and compare effective $/1k tokens for each option.
```
leo (support): note: if we do rollover, we need billing pipeline changes to persist per-customer credit ledger per quarter. that touches billing svc and metering. estimate: 2-3 sprints.
legal-ops: flagged — we need explicit language for rollover expiry, definitions of "seasonal spike", and termination proration. I'll draft clause.
anya (product): thanks. if finance modeling shows minimal delta between blended vs rollover w/ buffer, we prefer simpler (blended). otherwise recommend buffer+limited rollover. I'll schedule a 30m sync after ben posts numbers.
matt (sales): looping in ACME today — i'll set expectations that we're evaluating 2-3 approaches and will share numbers by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: Current public pricing refs: Reserved SKU monthly commit rate = $0.055 / 1k tokens; On-demand = $0.13 / 1k tokens; Burst premium suggestion default = 1.4x on-demand. (internal link: https://redwood.company/docs/pricing-models)
anya (product): perfect. last ask — include their expected model mix (chat/generation vs embeddings) if you can, that affects kernel/infra cost.
matt (sales): will do, sending usage breakdown after customer call.
anya (product): verdict: we need finance model + engineering estimate before shipping a recommended term to ACME. thanks all.
